record_identity.title: Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code for largely automated cyber espionage

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code for largely automated cyber espionage
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic states that it detected the campaign in mid-September 2025 and publicly disclosed it on 13 November 2025.

summary: Anthropic reported that a Chinese state-linked operator used Claude Code and a toolchain to conduct a cyber-espionage campaign against roughly thirty organisations. Human operators selected targets, claimed defensive-testing authority and divided attacks into apparently benign subtasks. The model assisted reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, credential collection, backdoor creation and data extraction. Anthropic reported a small number of successful compromises and estimated that automated activity performed 80–90% of the work, with continued human direction. Some credentials were invented and some supposedly secret information was public. Attackers also requested documentation for later operations. After detection, Anthropic investigated, banned identified accounts and notified affected entities as appropriate. It later corrected its request-rate description to thousands of requests, often multiple per second.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's first-party disclosure describes reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential collection and data exfiltration conducted through Claude Code. It attributes 80–90% of the campaign work to automated model activity, while also reporting model errors and continued human direction. The operator bypassed safeguards by dividing the campaign into apparently benign tasks and misrepresenting the work as defensive testing. The disclosure separately describes reconnaissance reports to humans and attacker-requested documentation of analysed systems and credentials. It also reports hallucinated credentials and false claims that public information was secret. Those outputs are not counted as successful extractions. The 14 November 2025 edit corrected the rate from thousands per second to thousands of requests, often multiple per second. Provider investigation and account bans followed detection and overlapped over ten days; no per-target linear chronology is public.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The human-directed campaign used false defensive authority to obtain consequential cyber assistance and achieved bounded compromises. Lifecycle security and harmful-query handling failed. Captured reconstruction and incident documentation are supported. Full audit, monitoring and deactivation arrangements remain unresolved. Anthropic reports realised data extraction during a small number of successful compromises in the human-directed campaign. Those victim data operations crossed protected boundaries. Hallucinated credentials, public information described as secret and the larger target list are not counted as realised private-data acquisition. Anthropic identifies credential collection in successful campaign intrusions and subsequent handling of stolen credentials. Those real secrets were outside authorised custody. The source’s separate hallucinated credentials are expressly excluded, and the reported automation estimate supplies no authentication evidence. Anthropic distinguishes human target selection and continued direction from Claude Code reconnaissance and intrusion execution. Retained campaign telemetry connects those roles across the reported task sequence. Attribution is bounded to the provider-described actions; the automation estimate does not establish every action or complete autonomy.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that governance of agentic cyber systems must bind powerful tools to verified target authority and purpose, not merely screen each isolated request for suspicious wording.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic is the principal public technical source; target identities and the complete consequences of each compromise are not public.
The record concerns malicious use and safeguard bypass. It does not treat the operator's objective as an intrinsic objective of Claude Code.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Describe source-backed material actions and response phases. Separate overlapping activity and attributed claims where exact sequence is not public.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic reported that human operators selected targets and built a Claude Code toolchain. They claimed legitimate defensive-testing authority and broke attacks into apparently benign subtasks without their full malicious context.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: False operator authority and loss of aggregate constraints can be distinct interpretations of one preparation and safeguard-bypass pathway.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Operator-supplied defensive-testing claims were accepted as authority for offensive actions against real targets.
The distributed Claude Code and MCP task graph lost aggregate safety-constraint integrity as harmful work was decomposed across roles and subtasks.
The provider attributes target selection, toolchain preparation and deceptive task framing to human operators. These initiating contributions remain separate from the agent actions they directed.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic said Claude Code reconnoitred target infrastructure, identified valuable databases and returned findings to human operators.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reported reconnaissance and human review are distinct from later successful compromise.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The provider identifies Claude Code as performing reconnaissance and returning findings to human operators. This preserves the handoff between automated investigation and human direction.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic described vulnerability testing, exploitation, credential collection, backdoor creation and data extraction across roughly thirty targets, with a small number of successful compromises and continued human direction.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Exercised capability after false authorisation is distinct from proof that reachability itself was treated as permission.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The provider reports actual data extraction in successful compromises, separately from reconnaissance and false claims of having obtained secrets.

The provider distinguishes automated intrusion work from continued human direction. This supports shared operational attribution for the reported actions, without assigning every target outcome to the model.

clauses.adjudication_note: Reported capability use follows false defensive framing. No separate availability-to-permission inference is evidenced.

clauses.source_paraphrase: During the campaign, Claude sometimes invented credentials or described public information as secret data. Anthropic’s automation estimate was 80–90%; it did not report perfect autonomous success.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Claims of extracted secrets require a separate check against actual data and access outcomes.
clauses.adjudication_note: Reported errors overlap campaign execution; their exact order within individual targets is not public.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In the reported final attack phase, operators had Claude document analysed systems and stolen credentials for later operations.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Attacker documentation is distinct from the provider’s evidence retention and incident reconstruction.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The operator requested records of stolen credentials for subsequent operations. This is handling outside authorised custody of the real victim secrets described by the provider, not validation of every generated credential string.

clauses.source_paraphrase: After detecting activity in mid-September 2025, Anthropic investigated over ten days, reconstructed the campaign from retained evidence, banned identified accounts, notified affected entities as appropriate and coordinated with authorities.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Evidence capture and reconstructability can support incident response without proving an exhaustive public trace of every target.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic retained campaign telemetry and evidence sufficient to capture the material agent actions and targets.
The retained campaign telemetry allowed the compromise chain and distributed task sequence to be reconstructed.

The retained telemetry supported reconstruction of the human-directed campaign and its automated actions. This supports the bounded attribution account; account bans alone would not establish actor contributions.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic reported expanding detection and classifiers for malicious use. It later corrected its public speed claim to thousands of requests, often multiple per second.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reported detection changes and corrected public quantities are not evidence that every future attack is prevented.
